'''Richard Gordon Swan''' ({{IPAc-en|s|w|ɑː|n}}; born 1933) is an American mathematician who is known for the [[Serre–Swan theorem]] relating the geometric notion of [[vector bundle]]s to the algebraic concept of [[projective module]]s,<ref>{{citation|first=P.|last=Manoharan|title=Generalized Swan's Theorem and its Application
|journal=[[Proceedings of the American Mathematical Society]]|volume=123|year=1995|pages=3219–3223|jstor=2160685|doi=10.2307/2160685|issue=10}}.</ref> and for the [[Swan representation]], an [[p-adic number|''l''-adic]] [[projective representation]] of a [[Galois group]].<ref>{{citation
 | last = Huber | first = R.
 | doi = 10.1515/crll.2001.063
 | journal = [[Journal für die Reine und Angewandte Mathematik]]
 | mr = 1856262
 | pages = 165–234
 | title = Swan representations associated with rigid analytic curves
 | volume = 2001
 | issue = 537
 | year = 2001}}.</ref> His work has mainly been in the area of [[algebraic K-theory|algebraic ''K''-theory]].

==Education and career==
As an undergraduate at [[Princeton University]], Swan was one of five winners in the [[William Lowell Putnam Mathematical Competition]] in 1952.<ref name="MMA">{{cite web |title=Putnam Competition Individual and Team Winners |url=http://www.maa.org/programs/maa-awards/putnam-competition-individual-and-team-winners |publisher=[[Mathematical Association of America]] |access-date=December 10, 2021 |archive-date=March 12, 2014 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140312205244/http://www.maa.org/programs/maa-awards/putnam-competition-individual-and-team-winners |url-status=dead }}</ref> He earned his Ph.D. in 1957 from [[Princeton University]] under the supervision of [[John Coleman Moore]].<ref name="mg">{{mathgenealogy|name=Richard Gordon Swan|id=6545}}</ref>

In 1969 he proved in full generality what is now known as the [[Cohomological dimension#Examples|Stallings–Swan theorem]].<ref>{{cite arXiv|author=Weigel, Thomas|author2=Zalesskii, Pavel|title=Virtually free pro-p products|year=2016|eprint=1305.4887|class=math.GR}}</ref><ref>{{cite journal|author=Swan, R. G.|year= 1969|title=Groups of cohomological dimension one|journal=[[Journal of Algebra]]|volume=12|issue=4|pages=585–610|doi=10.1016/0021-8693(69)90030-1|doi-access=free}}</ref> He is the Louis Block Professor Emeritus of Mathematics at the [[University of Chicago]].<ref>{{citation|url=http://www.math.uchicago.edu/people/|title=University of Chicago Mathematics Faculty Listing|access-date=2015-08-31}}.</ref>

His doctoral students at Chicago include [[Charles Weibel]], also known for his work in ''K''-theory.<ref name="mg"/>

Together with [[Otto Forster]] he proved the [[Forster–Swan theorem]].

==Awards and honors==
In 1970 Swan was awarded the [[American Mathematical Society]]'s [[Cole Prize]] in Algebra.
